title.zh: 卷四十三 蜀書十三 黃李呂馬王張傳
title.en: Volume 43: Book of Shu 13 - Biographies of Huang, Li, Lü, Ma, Wang, and Zhang
title.raw: 卷四十三 蜀書十三 黃李呂馬王張傳 Volume 43: Book of Shu 13 - Biographies of Huang, Li, Lü, Ma, Wang, and Zhang

sentences.zh: 黃權，字公衡，巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Huang Quan, whose courtesy name was Gongheng, was a man of Langzhong in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan, courtesy name Gongheng, came from Langzhong in Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，州牧劉璋召為主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a clerk in the commandery, and the provincial governor Liu Zhang summoned him to be chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served in the commandery administration; Provincial Governor Liu Zhang then appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時別駕張鬆建議，宜迎先主，使伐張魯。

translations.literal: At that time the junior administrator Zhang Song proposed that it was fitting to welcome the Vanguard Lord and send him to campaign against Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Deputy Governor Zhang Song urged Liu Zhang to invite Liu Bei westward and use him against Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 權諫曰：「左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君。

translations.literal: Quan remonstrated, saying, "The General of the Left has a fierce reputation; now that we have summoned him, if we wish to receive him as mere troops under our command, we will not satisfy his heart, and if we wish to treat him with the rites due a guest, then one state cannot accommodate two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan objected: "The General of the Left is famous as a fighting man. Having invited him in, if you treat him only as a subordinate army he will not be content; if you receive him as an honored guest, one realm cannot hold two masters.

sentences.zh: 若容有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。

translations.literal: If in accommodating him we gain the security of Mount Tai, then our lord will face the peril of piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: You may imagine that keeps you as secure as Mount Tai, but it will leave your master in peril stacked as high as eggs.

sentences.zh: 可但閉境，以待河清。

translations.literal: We may simply close the borders and await the clearing of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Better seal the passes and bide your time until Heaven sorts matters out.

sentences.zh: 」璋不聽，竟遣使迎先生，出權為廣漢長，及先主襲取益州，將帥分下郡縣。

translations.literal: " Zhang did not listen; in the end he sent envoys to welcome the Vanguard Lord, transferred Quan out to be magistrate of Guanghan, and when the Vanguard Lord seized Yi Province by surprise, the generals fanned out to take the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang refused to heed him and sent messengers to welcome Liu Bei, sidelining Huang Quan with an appointment as magistrate of Guanghan. When Liu Bei struck and took Yi Province, his commanders spread through the towns and districts.

sentences.zh: 郡縣風景附，權閉城堅守，須劉璋稽服，乃詣降先主。

translations.literal: The commanderies and counties submitted like wind and shadow; Quan closed the city gates and held firm, waited until Liu Zhang bowed in submission, and only then went to surrender to the Vanguard Lord.
translations.idiomatic: County after county went over to Liu Bei; Huang Quan shut his gates and held out until Liu Zhang had formally yielded, then he went in person to surrender to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主假權偏將軍。

translations.literal: The Vanguard Lord provisionally appointed Quan general of the left flank.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei named Huang Quan acting General of the Left Flank.

sentences.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：權既忠諫於主，又閉城拒守，得事君之禮。

translations.literal: < Xu Zhong comments: Quan had already offered loyal remonstrance to his lord and had shut the city gates to resist; he obtained the rites of serving a lord.
translations.idiomatic: < Xu Zhong comments: Huang Quan had spoken frankly for his master and then defended his walls—conduct fit for a faithful minister.

sentences.zh: 武王下車，封比干之墓，表商容之閭，所以大顯忠賢之士，而明示所貴之旨。

translations.literal: When the Martial King stepped down from his chariot, he sealed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane, thereby greatly displaying men who were loyal and worthy and clearly showing the intent of what he honored.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou entered the conquered Shang capital, he honored Bi Gan's grave and marked Shang Rong's lane—making plain whom he esteemed and giving loyal worthies their due.

sentences.zh: 先主假權將軍，善矣，然猶薄少，未足彰忠義之高節，而大勸為善者之心。〉

translations.literal: That the Vanguard Lord provisionally appointed Quan general was good, yet it was still slight and small, insufficient to display the lofty integrity of loyalty and righteousness and greatly encourage the hearts of those who would do good.>
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's provisional appointment of Huang Quan as general was decent as far as it went, yet it fell short of honoring such steadfast loyalty or firing others to virtue.

sentences.zh: 及曹公破張魯，魯走入巴中，權進曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao defeated Zhang Lu, Lu fled into Ba Commandery, and Quan advanced opinion, saying, "If we lose Hanzhong, then the Three Ba will not be stirred to vigor; this is cutting off Shu’s thigh and arm.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao defeated Zhang Lu and Lu fled into Ba, Huang Quan urged Liu Bei: "Lose Hanzhong and the Three Ba lose heart—you would be severing Shu’s arm and leg.

sentences.zh: 」於是先主以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯，魯已還南鄭，北降曹公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Vanguard Lord appointed Quan protector of the army and led the generals to welcome Lu; Lu had already returned to Nan Zheng and surrendered north to Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei then made Huang Quan chief of the Protectorate of the Army and marched to meet Zhang Lu, but Lu had already withdrawn to Nan Zheng and gone over to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they defeated Du Hu and Pu Hu, killed Xiahou Yuan, and held Hanzhong—all were Quan's original plans.
translations.idiomatic: The victories over Du Hu and Pu Hu, the slaying of Xiahou Yuan, and the seizure of Hanzhong all stemmed from Huang Quan's strategy.

sentences.zh: 後領益州刺史，徙佔河南。

translations.literal: Later he held the provincial governorship of Yi and moved his household south of the Yellow River (standard editions read ‘moved residence to Henan’ south of the river).
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Yi Province and resettled his family south of the Yellow River; standard editions use wording meaning ‘moved residence to Henan,’ i.e. south of the river.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬宣王深器之，問權曰：「蜀中有卿輩幾人？

translations.literal: Grand general Sima Yi of Xuande deeply esteemed him and asked Quan, saying, "In Shu how many men are there of your sort?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Sima Yi thought highly of him and asked, "How many men like you has Shu to offer?

sentences.zh: 」權笑而答曰：「不圖明公見顧之重也！

translations.literal: " Quan laughed and replied, saying, "I did not expect that you, enlightened lord, would regard me so heavily!
translations.idiomatic: " Huang Quan laughed and said, "I never dreamed Your Grace would think so well of me!

sentences.zh: 」宣王與諸葛亮書曰：「黃公衡，快士也，每坐起歎述足下，不去口實。

translations.literal: " Yi wrote to Zhuge Liang, saying, "Huang Gongheng is a forthright man; every time he rises from sitting he sighs and recounts you and never leaves off praising you.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi wrote to Zhuge Liang: "Huang Gongheng is a blunt, candid man—rise or sit, he never stops speaking well of you.

sentences.zh: 」景初三年，蜀延熙二年，權遷車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Jingchu, second year of Yanxi in Shu, Quan was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: " In Wei’s third year of Jingchu (239), Shu’s second year of Yanxi, Huang Quan was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors matching the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：魏明帝問權：「天下鼎立，當以何地為正？

translations.literal: < The Shu Ji records: Emperor Ming of Wei asked Quan, saying, "The realm stands like a tripod; which region should be deemed orthodox?
translations.idiomatic: < According to the Shu Ji, Wei Mingdi asked Huang Quan which of the three realms held legitimate mandate.

sentences.zh: 」權對曰：「當以天文為正。

translations.literal: " Quan replied, saying, "One should take celestial patterns as orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang Quan answered that legitimacy rests with what Heaven shows in the stars.

sentences.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文皇帝崩，吳、蜀二主平安，此其徵也。」〉

translations.literal: Formerly Mars guarded the heart [lodge] and Emperor Wen passed away, while the two lords of Wu and Shu were at peace; this is its omen." >
translations.idiomatic: When Mars stayed in the “heart” asterism, Emperor Wen of Wei died, yet the rulers of Wu and Shu were unharmed—a sign, he said, of where Heaven’s favor lay." >

sentences.zh: 明年卒，謚曰景侯。

translations.literal: The next year he died, posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and received the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子邕嗣、邕無子，絕。

translations.literal: Son Yong succeeded; Yong had no sons, and the line ended.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huang Yong inherited the marquisate; Yong left no heir, so the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 權留蜀子祟，為尚書郎，隨衛將軍諸葛瞻拒鄧艾。

translations.literal: Quan had left in Shu a son, Chong, who was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing; he followed General of the Guard Zhuge Zhan to resist Deng Ai.
translations.idiomatic: A son he had left in Shu, Huang Chong, served as a court secretary under General of the Guard Zhuge Zhan during the campaign against Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 到涪縣，瞻盤桓未近，祟屢勸瞻宜速行據險，無令敵得入平地。

translations.literal: When they reached Fu County, Zhan loitered and did not draw near; Chong repeatedly urged Zhan that he should quickly go to hold the defiles and not let the enemy get onto the flat land.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu, Zhuge Zhan hesitated and advanced slowly; Huang Chong urged him repeatedly to seize the mountain passes before the enemy could reach open ground.

sentences.zh: 瞻猶與未納，祟至於流涕。

translations.literal: Zhan still delayed and did not accept it; Chong reached the point of shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan still would not heed him, and Chong wept in frustration.

sentences.zh: 會艾長驅而前，瞻卻戰綿竹，祟帥厲軍士，期於必死，臨陣見殺。

translations.literal: When Ai drove straight forward, Zhan gave ground and fought at Mianzhu; Chong led and inspired the soldiers, looking to certain death, and was killed in the line of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai then advanced in force; Zhuge Zhan fell back to fight at Mianzhu. Huang Chong rallied the troops for a last stand and died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 先主薨，高定恣睢於越巂，雍闓跋扈於建寧，朱褒反叛於牂牁。

translations.literal: When the Vanguard Lord passed away, Gao Ding was unrestrained in Yuexi, Yong Kai was overbearing in Jianning, and Zhu Bao rebelled in Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei’s death, Gao Ding bullied the tribes in Yuexi, Yong Kai defied the court from Jianning, and Zhu Bao rose in rebellion in Zangke.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮南征，先由越俊，而恢案道向建寧。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Liang campaigned south, first by way of Yuejun (graph variant), while Hui pressed along the road toward Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang marched south through Yuexi while Li Hui advanced toward Jianning; this chapter writes ‘Yuejun’ where other editions read ‘Yuexi,’ the modern Liangshan region.

sentences.zh: 諸縣大相糾合，圍恢軍於昆明。

translations.literal: The counties largely gathered together and surrounded Hui's army at Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: County militias combined and pinned Li Hui’s force at Kunming.

sentences.zh: 時恢眾少敵倍，又未得亮聲息，繪謂南人曰：「官軍糧盡，欲規退還，吾中間久斥鄉里，乃今得旋，不能復北，欲還與汝等同計謀，故以誠相告。

translations.literal: At that time Hui's troops were few and the enemy doubled them, and moreover he had not obtained Liang's news; Hui (the text has 繪, likely 詐 'deceive') said to the southern people, "The government army's grain is exhausted and intends to plan withdrawal; I for long in the middle have been banished from my village; now I am able to turn back and cannot again go north; I wish to return and plot together with you like-minded ones; therefore with sincerity I inform you.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was outnumbered and cut off from Zhuge Liang’s word; feigning desertion, he told the southerners that government troops had run out of supplies and would retreat—that after years away from home he could finally turn south instead of north and wished to join their councils.

sentences.zh: 」南人信之，故圍守怠緩。

translations.literal: " The southern people believed it; therefore the siege defense became slack and slow.
translations.idiomatic: " They believed him, and their siege slackened.

sentences.zh: 於是恢出擊，大破之，追奔逐北，南至槃江，東接牂牁，與亮聲勢相連。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui went out and struck them, greatly defeating them, pursuing the fleeing and chasing the routed, south to the Pan River, east connecting to Zangke, and joined Liang's momentum and power.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui then sallied forth, routed them, and drove the fugitives south to the Pan River and east toward Zangke, linking up with Zhuge Liang’s advance.

sentences.zh: 南土平定，恢軍功居多。

translations.literal: The southern lands were pacified, and Hui's military merit was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: With the south subdued, most of the credit went to Li Hui’s column.

sentences.zh: 封漢興亭侯，加安漢將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as village marquis of Hanxing and added as general who pacifies Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Village Marquis of Hanxing and promoted to General Who Pacifies Han.

sentences.zh: 後軍還，南夷復叛，殺害守將。

translations.literal: Later when the army returned, the southern barbarians again rebelled and killed the defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, southern tribes rebelled again and slew the garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 恢身往撲討，鋤盡惡類，徙其豪帥於成都，賦出叟、濮耕牛戰馬金銀犀革，充繼軍資，於時費用不乏。

translations.literal: Hui personally went to strike and punish them, extirpating all evil sorts, moved their chieftains to Chengdu, and assessed out from the Sou and Pu oxen, war horses, gold, silver, and rhinoceros hide, filling and continuing military supplies, and at that time outlays were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui campaigned in person, extirpated the ringleaders, relocated their headmen to Chengdu, and levied cattle, horses, precious metals, and hides from the Sou and Pu peoples—keeping the army supplied without shortage.

sentences.zh: 建興七年，以交州屬吳，解恢刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jianxing, because Jiao Province was yielded to Wu, Hui was relieved of provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 7 (229), when Shu ceded suzerainty over Jiao Province to Wu, Li Hui was recalled from the governorship.

sentences.zh: 更領建寧太守，以還居本郡。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed prefect of Jianning and thereby returned to dwell in his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent appointment as Administrator of Jianning and so returned to govern his home region.

sentences.zh: 徙居漢中，九年卒。

translations.literal: He moved to dwell in Hanzhong and in the ninth year died.
translations.idiomatic: He later moved to Hanzhong and died in the ninth year (of Jianxing, 231).

sentences.zh: 子遺嗣，恢弟子球，羽林右部督，隨諸葛瞻拒鄧艾，臨陣授命，死於綿竹。

translations.literal: Son Yi succeeded; Hui's nephew Qiu, commander of the right division of the Feathered Forest, followed Zhuge Zhan to resist Deng Ai, accepted fate on the battlefield, and died at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Yi inherited the title; his nephew Li Qiu commanded the right wing of the imperial guard and died beside Zhuge Zhan fighting Deng Ai at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 凱答檄曰：

translations.literal: Kai replied to the proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai answered with this memorial:

sentences.zh: 天降喪亂，奸雄乘釁，天下切齒，萬國悲悼，臣妾大小，莫不思竭筋力，肝腦塗地，以除國難。

translations.literal: Heaven sent bereavement and turmoil; treacherous heroes seized the crack; all under heaven gnashed teeth; myriad states grieved; servants great and small none did not think to exhaust sinew and strength and smear liver and brains on the ground to remove the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent disaster and rebels seized their chance; every loyal heart raged, every household mourned, and high or low we longed to spend our strength—our lives if need be—to lift the realm from peril.

sentences.zh: 伏惟將軍世受漢思，以為當躬聚黨眾，率先啟行，上以報國家，下不負先人，書功竹帛，遺名千載。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the general for generations has received Han's grace; I thought you ought personally to gather party and multitude, take the lead and set out, above to repay the state, below not to betray forebears, inscribe merit on bamboo and silk, and leave a name for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your family has enjoyed Han favor for generations—you should rally your followers, march in the vanguard, repay the dynasty above and your ancestors below, and earn a place in the histories.

sentences.zh: 何期臣僕吳越，背本就末乎？

translations.literal: How could one expect to become servitors of Wu and Yue, turning the back on the root and pursuing the branch?
translations.idiomatic: How could you choose instead to play vassal to the Wu and Yue regimes—abandoning the trunk for a twig?

sentences.zh: 昔舜勤民事，隕於蒼梧，書籍嘉之，流聲無窮。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun toiled at the people's affairs and fell at Cangwu; the books praise him; his flowing fame is endless.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Shun wore himself out for the people and died at Cangwu—the classics honor him and his name still endures.

sentences.zh: 崩於江浦，何足可悲！

translations.literal: To die by the riverbank—what is worth grieving!
translations.idiomatic: Let lesser men perish on nameless riverbanks — beside Emperor Shun’s sacrifice that counts for nothing worth mourning.

sentences.zh: 文、武受命，成王乃平。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu received the mandate, and King Cheng then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Kings Wen and Wu received Heaven’s charge, and King Cheng finished securing the realm.

sentences.zh: 先帝龍興，海內望風，宰臣聰睿，自天降康。

translations.literal: The late emperor rose like a dragon; within the seas they looked to the wind; the chief ministers were wise and intelligent; from Heaven came prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Our late emperor rose like a dragon; the realm turned to him; wise ministers appeared and Heaven sent peace.

sentences.zh: 而將軍不睹盛衰之紀，成敗之符。

translations.literal: Yet the general does not observe the pattern of flourishing and decline, the tokens of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you refuse to read the signs of rise and fall, victory and defeat.

sentences.zh: 譬如野火在原，蹈覆河冰，火滅水泮，將何所依附？

translations.literal: It is like wildfire on the plain, treading cracked river ice; when the fire is extinguished and the water melts, where will you attach yourself?
translations.idiomatic: You are like someone crossing spring ice while grass fires rage—when the flames die and the ice breaks, what footing will you have?

sentences.zh: 囊者將軍先君雍候，造怨而封，竇融知興，歸志世祖，皆流名後葉，世歌其美。

translations.literal: Formerly the general's late father the marquis of Yong bore resentment yet was enfeoffed; Dou Rong knew the rising fortune and turned his will to Emperor Guangwu; all flowed their names to later ages and the age sings their beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Your father the Marquis of Yong once turned hostility into enfeoffment; Dou Rong read the times and pledged to Emperor Guangwu—both won lasting fame because they chose the rising house.

sentences.zh: 今諸葛丞相英才挺出，深睹未萌，受遺託孤，翊贊季興，與眾無忌，錄功忘瑕。

translations.literal: Now Chancellor Zhuge's outstanding talent arose; he deeply saw what had not yet sprouted; he received the testament and was entrusted with the orphan; he assists and aids the secondary revival; with the multitude he has no jealousy; he records merit and forgets flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang is a genius who reads trouble before it shows; he holds the late emperor’s mandate, steadies the restoration, shares credit openly, and rewards merit while overlooking fault.

sentences.zh: 將軍若能翻然改圖，易跡更步，古人不難追，鄙土何足宰哉！

translations.literal: If the general can suddenly change plans, alter tracks and change steps, the ancients are not hard to follow—how could mean territory be worth ruling!
translations.idiomatic: If you reverse course now, you may still match the ancients in loyalty—this poor soil of Yongchang is hardly worth clinging to as a petty king.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞楚國不恭，齊桓是責，夫差僭號，晉人不長。

translations.literal: I have heard that when Chu was disrespectful, Duke Huan of Qi was the one who punished; Fuchai presumptuously assumed title, and the men of Jin did not long endure it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu defied the league, Duke Huan of Qi called them to account; when King Fuchai usurped royal style, the lords of Jin did not let it pass for long.

sentences.zh: 況臣與非主，誰肯歸之邪？

translations.literal: How much more when a subject serves a lord who is not right—who would return to him?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should we serve a lord who lacks legitimacy—who would follow such a man?

sentences.zh: 竊惟古義，臣無越境之交，是以前後有來無往。

translations.literal: I privately consider the ancient meaning: a minister has no interstate dealings beyond the border; therefore before and after there were those who came but none who went.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient protocol ministers do not negotiate across borders without leave—hence your messengers came here with no reply from us.

sentences.zh: 重承告示，發憤忘食，故略陳所懷，惟將軍察焉。

translations.literal: Again receiving your notice, I was stirred and forgot eating; therefore I briefly set forth what I hold in my heart; may the general examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter stirred me so deeply I forgot my meal; I lay out my thoughts plainly for your judgment.

sentences.zh: 凱威恩內著，為郡中所信，故能全其節。

translations.literal: Kai's awesomeness and favor were manifest within, and the commandery believed in him; therefore he was able to preserve his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai’s authority and kindness were felt at home, and the commandery trusted him, so he could keep his honor intact.

sentences.zh: 及丞相亮南征討闓，既發在道，而闓已為高定部曲所殺。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang campaigned south to attack Yong Kai (graph variant), having already set out on the road, Kai had already been killed by Gao Ding's personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang had barely marched south against Yong Kai when word came that Gao Ding’s men had already killed him; this chapter writes Yong Kai’s name with an alternate graph.

sentences.zh: 亮至南，上表曰：「永昌郡吏呂凱、府丞王伉等，執忠絕域，十有餘年，雍闓、高定逼其東北，而凱等守義不與交通。

translations.literal: When Liang reached the south he submitted a memorial, saying, "The Yongchang commandery clerks Lü Kai, prefectural aide Wang Kang, and others, holding loyalty in a remote region for more than ten years—Yong Kai and Gao Ding pressed them from northeast—yet Kai and the others kept righteousness and did not communicate with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang arrived he memorialized: "Clerk Lü Kai of Yongchang, Assistant Wang Kang, and their comrades have kept faith in a remote border for more than a decade, cut off to the northeast by Yong Kai and Gao Ding, yet they never dealt with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 臣不意永昌風俗敦直乃爾！

translations.literal: I did not expect Yongchang's customs to be so honest and upright!
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined Yongchang still harbored such steadfast integrity!

sentences.zh: 」以凱為雲南太守，封陽遷亭侯，會為叛夷所害，子祥嗣。

translations.literal: " He appointed Kai prefect of Yunnan and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yangqian; Kai was harmed by rebel barbarians, and son Xiang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed Lü Kai Administrator of Yunnan and enfeoffed him as Village Marquis of Yangqian; when tribal rebels later murdered him, his son Lü Xiang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 而王伉亦封亭侯，為永昌太守。

translations.literal: And Wang Kang was also enfeoffed as village marquis and became prefect of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang too received a village marquisate and was appointed Administrator of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀世譜》曰：呂祥後為晉南夷校尉，祥子及孫世為永昌太守。

translations.literal: < The Shu Shifu records: Lü Xiang later became Jin's Colonel Who Pacifies the Southern Barbarians; Xiang's sons and grandsons for generations were prefects of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: < According to the Shu genealogical tables, Lü Xiang later served Jin as Colonel of the Southern Yi; his descendants held Yongchang for generations.

sentences.zh: 李雄破寧州，諸呂不肯附，舉郡固守。

translations.literal: When Li Xiong broke Ning Province, the various Lüs were unwilling to submit and raised the commandery to firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiong overran Ningzhou, the Lü clan refused submission and defended the whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 王伉等亦守正節。〉

translations.literal: Wang Kang and others also kept correct integrity.>
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang and his fellows likewise died loyal to the end.>

sentences.zh: 王平字子均，巴西宕渠人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ping, courtesy name Zijun, was a man of Dangqu in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping, courtesy name Zijun, came from Dangqu in Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本養外家何氏。

translations.literal: Originally he was raised by his mother's family the He's.
translations.idiomatic: He had been raised in his maternal He family.

sentences.zh: 後復姓王。

translations.literal: Later he restored the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He later took back the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 隨杜濩、樸胡詣洛陽，假校尉，從曹公征漢中，因降先主，拜牙門將、裨將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Du Hu and Pu Hu to Luoyang, was provisionally appointed colonel, followed Duke Cao on the Hanzhong campaign, and thereby surrendered to the Vanguard Lord; he was appointed general of the barracks gate and subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Du Hu and Pu Hu to Luoyang, received a brevet colonel’s rank, and joined Cao Cao’s Hanzhong campaign, then went over to Liu Bei and was made a camp-gate general and subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 建興六年，屬參軍馬謖先鋒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing he was attached to army adviser Ma Su as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 6 (228) he served under Army Adviser Ma Su as an advance officer.

sentences.zh: 謖捨水上山，舉措煩擾，平連規諫謖，謖不能用，大敗於街亭。

translations.literal: Su abandoned the water and went up the mountain; his dispositions were confused and erratic; Ping remonstrated with him again and again in due form; Su was unable to heed it, and they were greatly defeated at Jieting.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Su camped on the hills and gave up the water, throwing the army into confusion. Wang Ping warned him again and again, but Ma Su ignored the advice and was crushed at Jieting.

sentences.zh: 眾盡星散，惟平所領千人鳴鼓自持，魏將張郃疑其伏兵，不往逼也。

translations.literal: The host all scattered like stars; only the thousand men Ping led beat drums and held themselves; Wei general Zhang He suspected ambush and did not go to press them.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke and ran, but Wang Ping’s thousand men kept up a steady drumbeat; Zhang He suspected a trap and dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 於是平徐徐收合諸營遺迸，率將士而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ping slowly gathered and combined the various camps' scattered remnants and led the generals and soldiers back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping then regrouped the stragglers from every camp and marched the men home in good order.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮既誅馬謖及將軍張休、李盛，奪將軍黃襲等兵。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang, having executed Ma Su and generals Zhang Xiu and Li Sheng, stripped the troops of generals like Huang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang executed Ma Su, Zhang Xiu, and Li Sheng, he stripped other generals such as Huang Xi of their commands.

sentences.zh: 平特見崇顯，加拜參軍，統五部兼當營事，進位討寇將軍，封亭侯。

translations.literal: Ping was uniquely honored and displayed; he was additionally appointed army adviser, commanded five divisions while concurrently managing camp affairs, advanced to general who punishes bandits, and enfeoffed as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping alone was singled out for praise—promoted to army adviser, given five brigades with charge of camp affairs, raised to General Who Punishes Raiders, and made a village marquis.

sentences.zh: 九年，亮圍祁山，平別守南圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liang besieged Mount Qi; Ping separately guarded the southern siege.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 9 (231), while Zhuge Liang besieged Mount Qi, Wang Ping held the southern perimeter.

sentences.zh: 魏大將軍司馬宣王攻亮，張郃攻平，平堅守不動，郃不能克。

translations.literal: Wei grand general Sima Yi attacked Liang; Zhang He attacked Ping; Ping firmly guarded and did not move; He could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi struck Zhuge Liang’s main force, Zhang He assaulted Wang Ping’s sector; Wang Ping held firm and Zhang He could not break him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，亮卒於武功，軍退還，魏延作亂，一戰而敗，平之功也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Liang died at Wugong; when the army withdrew and returned, Wei Yan made rebellion; they were defeated in one battle—this was Ping's merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 12 (234), after Zhuge Liang died at Wugong and the army withdrew, Wei Yan mutinied and was crushed in a single engagement—credit belonged to Wang Ping.

sentences.zh: 遷後典軍、安漢將軍，副車騎將軍吳壹住漢中，又領軍漢中太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant to the camp marshal and general who pacifies Han, subordinate to general of chariots and cavalry Wu Yi garrisoning Hanzhong, and also acting as military overseer and prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Army and General Who Pacifies Han, second to General of Chariots and Cavalry Wu Yi in the Hanzhong garrison, while holding concurrent authority as Administrator of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進封安漢侯，代壹督漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was advanced and enfeoffed as marquis who pacifies Han, replacing Yi as supervisor of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 15 (237) he was elevated to Marquis Who Pacifies Han and succeeded Wu Yi as commander at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年，大將軍蔣琬住沔陽，平更為前護軍，署琬府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxi the grand general Jiang Wan garrisoned Mianyang; Ping was further made forward protector of the army and managed Wan's office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 1 (238), with Grand General Jiang Wan posted at Mianyang, Wang Ping became Forward Protector of the Army and managed affairs in Jiang Wan’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，琬還住涪，拜平前監軍、鎮北大將軍，統漢中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Wan returned to garrison Fu; Ping was appointed forward overseer of the army and general who guards the north, commanding Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 6 (243), when Jiang Wan moved his headquarters to Fu, Wang Ping was named Forward Army Inspector and Grand General Who Guards the North, with overall command of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 七年春，魏大將軍曹爽率步騎十餘萬向漢川，前鋒已在駱谷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, Wei grand general Cao Shuang led more than a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry toward the Han River plain; the vanguard was already at Lu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yanxi 7 (244), Wei Grand General Cao Shuang advanced on Hanzhong with well over a hundred thousand foot and horse; his van had already entered Lu Valley.

sentences.zh: 時漢中守兵不滿三萬，諸將大驚。

translations.literal: At that time Hanzhong's defending troops did not reach thirty thousand; the generals were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than thirty thousand men held Hanzhong, and the commanders panicked.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今力不足以拒敵，聽當固守漢、樂二城，遇賊令入，比爾間，涪軍足得救關。

translations.literal: Some said, "Now strength is insufficient to resist the enemy; we ought simply to firmly guard the two cities of Han and Le, encounter the bandits and let them enter; in the meantime among ourselves Fu's army will be enough to rescue the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged: "We cannot meet them in the field—hold Hanxing and Lecheng and let the enemy through the mountains; reinforcements from Fu can relieve the passes before it is too late.

sentences.zh: 」平曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Ping said, "This is not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Ping replied, "That would be a mistake.

sentences.zh: 漢中去涪垂千里。

translations.literal: Hanzhong is nearly a thousand li from Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong lies almost a thousand li from Fu.

sentences.zh: 賊若得關，便為禍也。

translations.literal: If the bandits obtain the passes, then it becomes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If they seize the passes, disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 今宜先遣劉護軍、杜參軍據興勢，平為後拒。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting first to send Protector Liu and Army Adviser Du to hold Xingshi; Ping will be rear ward.
translations.idiomatic: Send Protector of the Army Liu and Army Adviser Du to seize Xingshi first—I will cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 若賊分向黃金，平率千人下自臨之，比爾間，涪軍行至，此計之上也。

translations.literal: If the bandits divide toward Huangjin, Ping will lead a thousand men down to face them personally; in the meantime among ourselves Fu's army will arrive—this is the best of plans.
translations.idiomatic: If they split toward Huangjin, I will take a thousand men downhill to hold them; by then Fu’s relief column will arrive—the soundest plan.

sentences.zh: 」惟護軍劉敏與平意同，即便施行。

translations.literal: " Only Protector Liu Min agreed with Ping's intent, and immediately they implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: " Only Protector of the Army Liu Min agreed with Wang Ping, and they carried it out at once.

sentences.zh: 涪諸軍及費禕自成都相繼而至，魏軍退還，如平本策。

translations.literal: The various armies at Fu and Fei Yi from Chengdu arrived one after another; the Wei army withdrew and returned, according to Ping's original strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements from Fu and Fei Yi’s troops from Chengdu arrived in succession; the Wei army withdrew exactly as Wang Ping had predicted.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄧芝在東，馬忠在南，平在北境，咸著名跡。

translations.literal: At this time Deng Zhi was in the east, Ma Zhong in the south, Ping on the northern border; all were noted for famous traces.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi held the east, Ma Zhong the south, Wang Ping the northern frontier—each won renown in his theater.

sentences.zh: 平生長戎旅，手不能書，其所識不過十字，而口授作書，皆有意理。

translations.literal: Ping grew up in the army camp; his hands could not write; what he recognized did not exceed ten characters, yet dictating writing, all had meaningful coherence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping grew up in the ranks; he could barely write a handful of characters, yet dictating letters to scribes he always produced clear, sensible prose.

sentences.zh: 使人讀《史》、《漢》諸紀傳，聽之，備知其大義，往往論說不失其指。

translations.literal: He had men read the Records and Han various annals and biographies; listening, he fully knew their great meaning; often in discussion he did not miss their point.
translations.idiomatic: He had aides read him the Shiji and Hanshu; he grasped their main arguments and could discuss them without missing the point.

sentences.zh: 遵履法度，言不戲諺，從朝至夕，端坐徹日，懷無武將之體。

translations.literal: He observed and trod law and measure; his speech was not jesting proverb; from morning to evening he sat upright through the day; in bearing he had no martial general's deportment.
translations.idiomatic: He observed regulations strictly, never indulged in coarse soldier’s humor, and sat bolt upright from dawn to dusk—yet carried himself without the swagger usual in fighting men.

sentences.zh: 然性狹侵疑，為人自輕，以此為損焉。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was narrow, invasive, and suspicious; as a man he belittled himself; by this there was harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was narrow-minded and quick to take offense, prone to sell himself short—a flaw in an otherwise formidable commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，子訓嗣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; son Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Yanxi (248); his son Wang Xun inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 初，平同郡漢昌句

translations.literal: Formerly, from the same commandery as Ping, Han Chang—sentence breaks mid-name Gou—
translations.idiomatic: In Wang Ping’s home commandery lived Gou—his personal name is split across sentences in this edition—

sentences.zh: 〈句古候反〉

translations.literal: < Note on pronunciation: Gou, ancient hou fan >
translations.idiomatic: < Phonetic gloss: the surname Gou is read with the ‘hou’ rime >

sentences.zh: 忠勇寬厚，數有戰功，功名爵位亞平，官至左將軍，封宕渠侯。

translations.literal: Loyal, brave, generous, and thick—he repeatedly had battle merit; merit fame and noble rank were second to Ping; office reached general of the left; enfeoffed as marquis of Dangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, brave, and steady in temper, he won repeated battlefield honors. His fame and titles stood just below Wang Ping’s; he rose to General of the Left and Marquis of Dangqu.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：後張翼、廖化並為大將軍，時人語曰：「前有王、句，後有張、廖。」〉

translations.literal: < The Huayang Guo Zhi records: Later Zhang Yi and Liao Hua both became grand generals; people of the time said, "Before there were Wang and Gou; after there are Zhang and Liao." >
translations.idiomatic: < The Huayang Guo Zhi notes that when Zhang Yi and Liao Hua later became grand generals, folk rhyme had it: ‘Wang and Gou led the way; Zhang and Liao followed.’ >

sentences.zh: 張嶷字伯岐，巴郡南充國人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ni, courtesy name Boqi, was a man of Nanchong in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni, courtesy name Boqi, came from Nanchong in Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷出自孤微，而少有通壯之節。〉

translations.literal: < The Biographies of the Elders of Yi records: Ni came from obscure and humble origins, yet in youth had broadly vigorous integrity.>
translations.idiomatic: < The Yi-region elders’ tradition calls Zhang Ni a man of humble birth who showed stalwart resolve even as a youth.>

sentences.zh: 弱冠為縣功曹。

translations.literal: At his capping he became county merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he served as merit clerk of his county.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀之際，山寇攻縣，縣長捐家逃亡，嶷冒白刃，攜負夫人，夫人得免。

translations.literal: When the Vanguard Lord pacified Shu, mountain bandits attacked the county; the county chief abandoned his household and fled; Ni braved bare blades, carried the lady on his back on his shoulders, and the lady obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei was securing Shu, hill bandits stormed the county; the magistrate fled and abandoned his household. Zhang Ni ran through blade strokes and bore his superior’s wife to safety.

sentences.zh: 由是顯名，州召為從事。

translations.literal: Thereby his name became eminent; the province summoned him as attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame for it and the provincial administration appointed him attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 時郡內士人龔祿、姚冑位二千石，當世有聲名，皆與嶷友善。

translations.literal: At that time within the commandery the gentlemen Gong Lu and Yao Zhou held two-thousand-bushel rank and had reputation in the generation; all were friendly with Ni.
translations.idiomatic: County notables such as Gong Lu and Yao Zhou, senior officials with eminent reputations, all befriended him.

sentences.zh: 建興五年，丞相亮北住漢中，廣漢綿竹山賊張慕等鈔盜軍資，劫略吏民，嶷以都尉將兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianxing the Chancellor Liang garrisoned Hanzhong to the north; in Guanghan the Mianzhu mountain bandits Zhang Mu and others plundered military supplies and kidnapped officials and people; Ni as colonel led troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 5 (227), while Zhuge Liang held Hanzhong, the Mianzhu bandits led by Zhang Mu raided army stores and civilians. Zhang Ni, as a colonel, took troops against them.

sentences.zh: 嶷度其鳥散，難以戰禽。

translations.literal: Ni estimated that they would scatter like birds and be hard to catch in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni knew they would splinter like a flock of birds and could not be run down in open battle.

sentences.zh: 乃詐與和親，剋期置酒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feigned peace and kinship, set a day, and prepared wine.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned a marriage alliance, set a date, and invited them to a feast.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，嶷身率左右，因斬慕等五十餘級，渠帥悉珍。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, Ni personally led his attendants and thereupon beheaded Mu and more than fifty heads; the chieftains were all exterminated (text 珍, likely 殄).
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was flowing, Zhang Ni took his men in and cut down Zhang Mu and more than fifty others, wiping out the ringleaders (the text has a graph that should read ‘exterminate’).

sentences.zh: 尋其餘類，旬日清泰。

translations.literal: He tracked their remaining sorts; in ten days all was clear and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted down the rest; within ten days the district was quiet.

sentences.zh: 後得疾病困篤，家素貧匱。

translations.literal: Later he contracted illness severely grave; his household was always poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell gravely ill while his family remained desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守蜀郡何祗，名為通厚，嶷宿與疏闊，乃自輿詣祗，託以治疾。

translations.literal: The Guanghan prefect He Zhi of Shu Commandery was named as comprehending and generous; Ni had long been distant from him, yet personally rode in a litter to Zhi and entrusted him with treating the illness.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi of Guanghan had a reputation for generosity though Zhang Ni barely knew him; Zhang Ni had himself carried to He Zhi’s door and begged him for treatment.

sentences.zh: 祗傾托醫療，數年除愈。

translations.literal: Zhi devoted himself to medical treatment; in several years he removed and cured it.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi threw every resource into his care, and after several years Zhang Ni recovered.

sentences.zh: 其黨道信義皆此類也。

translations.literal: His party-path of faith and righteousness was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His circle honored loyalty and good faith in just this way.

sentences.zh: 拜為牙門將，屬馬忠，北討汶山叛羌，南平四郡蠻夷，輒有籌畫戰克之功。

translations.literal: He was appointed general of the barracks gate, attached to Ma Zhong; north he campaigned against the rebellious Qiang of Wenshan, south he pacified the four commanderies' barbarians and Yi—always there was planning and battle victory merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to camp-gate general under Ma Zhong, campaigned north against the Wenshan Qiang and south through the four southern commanderies, winning every engagement he planned.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷受兵馬三百人，隨馬忠討叛羌。

translations.literal: < The Biographies of the Elders of Yi records: Ni received three hundred soldiers and horses and followed Ma Zhong to punish rebellious Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: < The Yi elders’ tradition records that Zhang Ni took three hundred horse and foot under Ma Zhong against the rebel Qiang.

sentences.zh: 嶷別督數營在先，至他裡。

translations.literal: Ni separately supervised several camps in the van and arrived at Tali.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni led several camps on the advance guard and reached the settlement of Tali.

sentences.zh: 邑所在高峻，嶷隨山立上四五里。

translations.literal: The town site was high and steep; Ni climbed along the mountain four or five li upward.
translations.idiomatic: The town sat on a high ridge; Zhang Ni climbed four or five li of mountain trail.

sentences.zh: 羌於要厄作石門，於門上施床，積石於其上，過者下石槌擊之，無不糜爛。

translations.literal: The Qiang at a strategic choke made a stone gate; on the gate they set platforms and piled stones on them; those who passed below they struck with stone hammers—none did not become mashed and rotten.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang walled a stone gate across the defile, piled rocks on ledges above the portal, and smashed every traveler beneath with stone hammers—no one survived.

sentences.zh: 嶷度不可得攻，乃使譯告曉之曰：「汝汶山諸種反叛，傷害良善，天子命將討滅惡類。

translations.literal: Ni estimated it could not be assaulted; thereupon he sent interpreters to announce and enlighten them, saying, "You Wenshan various sorts rebel, harm the good; the Son of Heaven ordered generals to punish and exterminate evil kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no way to storm the pass, Zhang Ni sent interpreters: "Your Wenshan tribes have rebelled and preyed on the innocent; the emperor has sent armies to destroy such evil.

sentences.zh: 汝等若稽顙過軍，資給糧費，福祿永隆，其報百倍。

translations.literal: If you knock forehead and pass the army, supplying grain expense, fortune and salary will forever rise; the reward will be a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Bow before our host, furnish grain and supplies, and your rewards will multiply a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 若終不從，大兵致誅，雷擊電下，雖追悔之，亦無益也。

translations.literal: If to the end you do not obey, great troops will bring execution; thunder strike lightning descend—though afterward you regret it, it will also be without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse, and the full army will fall on you like thunder—too late then for regret.

sentences.zh: 」耆帥得命，即出詣嶷，給糧過軍。

translations.literal: " The elder chief received the command, immediately came out to Ni, and supplied grain for the army to pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The headman accepted the terms, came down to Zhang Ni, and fed the column through the pass.

sentences.zh: 軍前討餘種，餘種聞他裡已下，悉恐怖失所，或迎軍出降，或奔竄山谷，放兵攻擊，軍以克捷。

translations.literal: The army advanced to punish the remaining sorts; the remaining sorts heard Tali had fallen and all were terrified and lost place; some welcomed the army and came out to surrender, some fled into mountain valleys; releasing troops they attacked; the army thereby achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: The army then rolled up the other bands: hearing Tali had fallen, they panicked—some surrendered to the columns, some scattered into the hills; Zhang Ni’s men pursued and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 後南夷劉冑又反，以馬忠為督庲降討冑，嶷复屬焉，戰鬥常冠軍首，遂斬冑。

translations.literal: Later the southern Yi Liu Zhou again rebelled; Ma Zhong was made supervisor of Zhangxi to punish Zhou; Ni again was attached; in battle he always ranked first in the army and thereupon beheaded Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern leader Liu Zhou rose again, Ma Zhong took command of the Zhangxi campaign and Zhang Ni fought under him, always leading the van until Zhou was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 平南事訖，牂牁興古獠種復反，忠令嶷領諸營往討，嶷內招降得二千人，悉傳詣漢中。〉

translations.literal: When the southern pacification was finished, the Zangke and Xinggu Liao sorts again rebelled; Zhong ordered Ni to lead the various camps to go punish; Ni inwardly summoned surrender and obtained two thousand men, all transported to Hanzhong.>
translations.idiomatic: After the south was quiet, tribes in Zangke and Xinggu rebelled again; Ma Zhong sent Zhang Ni at the head of several camps. Zhang Ni won two thousand surrendering tribesmen and sent them all to Hanzhong.>

sentences.zh: 十四年，武都氐王苻健請降，遣將軍張尉往迎，過期不到，大將軍蔣琬深以為念。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Di king of Wudu, Fu Jian, requested surrender; they sent General Zhang Wei to go welcome; past the deadline he did not arrive; Grand General Jiang Wan deeply took it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 14 (251) the Wudu Di chieftain Fu Jian offered to defect; Shu dispatched General Zhang Wei to escort him. When the escort failed to appear on time, Jiang Wan grew deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 嶷平之曰：「苻健求附款至，必無他變。

translations.literal: Ni calmly said, "Fu Jian seeking attachment is sincere in intent; assuredly there is no other change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni reassured him: "Fu Jian’s offer of allegiance is sincere; nothing else is afoot.

sentences.zh: 素聞健弟狡黠，又夷狄不能同功，將有乖離，是以稽留耳。

translations.literal: I have long heard Jian's younger brother is crafty; moreover barbarians cannot share merit together—there will be estrangement; therefore delay.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother is treacherous, and frontier peoples seldom pull together—some split was inevitable, hence the delay.

sentences.zh: 」數日，問至，健弟果將四百戶就魏，獨健來從。

translations.literal: " Several days later, inquiry arrived; Jian's younger brother indeed led four hundred households to Wei; only Jian came to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later word arrived: the brother had taken four hundred households to Wei, while Fu Jian alone came over to Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，越巂郡自丞相亮討高定之後，叟夷數反，殺太守龔祿、焦璜，是後太守不敢之郡，只住安定縣，去郡八百餘里，其郡徒有名而已。

translations.literal: Formerly, Yuexi Commandery since Chancellor Liang punished Gao Ding, the Sou Yi repeatedly rebelled, killing prefects Gong Lu and Jiao Huang; afterward prefects dared not go to the commandery, only dwelt in Anding County, more than eight hundred li from the commandery—the commandery had only a name.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s campaign against Gao Ding, the Sou tribes of Yuexi rose repeatedly, killing Administrators Gong Lu and Jiao Huang. Later appointees never dared enter the seat, camping eight hundred li away at Anding—the commandery existed on paper only.

sentences.zh: 時論欲復舊郡，除嶷為越巂太守，嶷將所領往之郡，誘以恩情，蠻夷皆服，頗來降附。

translations.literal: Current opinion wished to restore the old commandery; Ni was appointed prefect of Yuexi; Ni led those he commanded and went to the commandery, enticing with grace affection; the barbarians and Yi all submitted; quite many came to surrender and attach.
translations.idiomatic: The court resolved to restore the old seat and named Zhang Ni Administrator. He marched his command into the territory, winning people with kindness until many tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 北徼捉馬最驍勁，不承節度，嶷乃往討，生縛其帥魏狼。

translations.literal: The northern frontier Zhuoma were most fierce and strong; they did not accept regulation; Ni thereupon went to punish them and bound alive their chief Wei Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuoma horsemen on the northern marches were violent and defied orders; Zhang Ni attacked, took their chief Wei Lang alive, and bound him.

sentences.zh: 又解縱告喻，使招懷餘類。

translations.literal: Again he released and informed them, sending them to summon and cherish remaining sorts.
translations.idiomatic: He then freed Wei Lang and used him to bring the rest of the tribe to terms.

sentences.zh: 表拜狼為邑侯，種落三千餘戶皆安土供職。

translations.literal: He submitted and appointed Lang as village marquis; the tribes and settlements more than three thousand households all settled on the land and performed duty.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to enfeoff Wei Lang as a village marquis; more than three thousand households settled down and paid their dues.

sentences.zh: 諸種聞之，多漸降服。

translations.literal: The various sorts hearing it, many gradually surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Other clans heard of it and steadily came over.

sentences.zh: 嶷以功賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Ni for merit was granted noble rank as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit Zhang Ni received the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 蘇祁邑君冬逢、逢弟魄渠等，已降復反。

translations.literal: The Suqi district lord Dong Feng and Feng's younger brother Po Qu and others had surrendered yet again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Suqi headmen Dong Feng and his brother Po Qu had submitted once, then rose again.

sentences.zh: 嶷誅逢。

translations.literal: Ni executed Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni executed Dong Feng.

sentences.zh: 逢妻，旄牛王女，嶷以計原之。

translations.literal: Feng's wife was the Maoniu king's daughter; Ni by stratagem forgave her.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Feng’s wife was a princess of the Maoniu king; Zhang Ni spared her by design.

sentences.zh: 而渠逃入西徼。

translations.literal: But Qu fled into the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Po Qu fled into the western hills.

sentences.zh: 渠剛猛捷悍，為諸種深所畏憚，遣所親二人詐降嶷，實取消息。

translations.literal: Qu was fierce, fierce, swift, and hardy; he was deeply feared by the various sorts; he sent two intimate attendants to feign surrender to Ni, actually to gather news.
translations.idiomatic: Po Qu was fierce and feared by every tribe; he sent two trusted men under false surrender to spy on Zhang Ni.

sentences.zh: 嶷覺之，許以重賞，使為反間，二人遂合謀殺渠。

translations.literal: Ni perceived it, promised heavy reward, made them serve as counter-spies; the two men thereupon conspired together and killed Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni saw through it, bought them with rich promises, and turned them as double agents—they murdered Po Qu together.

sentences.zh: 渠死，諸種皆安。

translations.literal: When Qu died, the various sorts were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With Po Qu dead the tribes quieted down.

sentences.zh: 又斯都耆帥李求承昔手殺龔祿，嶷求募捕得，數其宿惡而誅之。

translations.literal: Also the Sidu elder chief Li Qiucheng formerly personally killed Gong Lu; Ni sought and recruited capture and obtained him, enumerated his long-standing evils and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Sidu leader Li Qiucheng had once murdered Gong Lu with his own hand; Zhang Ni had him hunted down, listed his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 始嶷以郡郛宇頹壞，更築小塢。

translations.literal: At first Ni because the commandery rampart halls were ruined and collapsed, built anew a small walled enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: At first, finding the commandery walls ruined, Zhang Ni built a smaller fortified compound.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，徙還故郡，繕治城郭，夷種男女莫不致力。』

translations.literal: In office three years, he was transferred back to the former commandery, repaired and governed city walls; barbarian sorts male and female none did not exert effort.』
translations.idiomatic: After three years he returned to his former seat, rebuilt the walls, and men and women of every tribe labored beside him.』

sentences.zh: 定莋、台登、卑水三縣去郡三百餘里，舊出鹽鐵及漆，而夷徼久自固食。

translations.literal: The three counties Dingzuo, Taideng, and Beishui were more than three hundred li from the commandery; formerly they produced salt, iron, and lacquer, yet the Yi frontier long held them for their own food.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzuo, Taideng, and Beishui lay three hundred li from the seat, rich in salt, iron, and lacquer that frontier tribes had kept for themselves for generations.

sentences.zh: 嶷率所領奪取，署長吏焉。

translations.literal: Ni led those he commanded to seize them and appointed senior clerks there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni seized them by force and installed his own magistrates.

sentences.zh: 嶷之到定莋，定莋率豪狼岑，盤木王舅，甚為蠻夷所信任，忿嶷自侵，不自來詣。

translations.literal: When Ni arrived at Dingzuo, Dingzuo's chief magnate Langcen, uncle by marriage of the Panmu king, was greatly trusted by barbarians and Yi; resenting Ni's invasion of himself, he did not himself come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzuo the magnate Langcen—uncle of the Panmu king—was influential among the tribes and refused to answer Zhang Ni’s summons, resenting what he saw as intrusion.

sentences.zh: 嶷使壯士數十直往收致，撻而殺之，持屍還種，厚加賞賜。

translations.literal: Ni sent several tens of stalwarts straight to seize and bring him, flogged and killed him, carried the corpse back to the sorts, and generously added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni sent dozens of picked men to seize Langcen, executed him after a flogging, returned the body to his people, and lavished gifts on them.

sentences.zh: 喻以狼岑之惡，且曰：「無得妄動，動即殄矣！

translations.literal: He enlightened them with Langcen's evil and said, "Do not dare move rashly; move and you will be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: He explained Langcen’s crimes and warned: "Stay still—any move will mean your annihilation!

sentences.zh: 」種類咸面縛謝過。

translations.literal: " The sorts and kinds all bound their faces forward and apologized for faults.
translations.idiomatic: " The clans came bound and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 嶷殺午饗宴，重申恩信。

translations.literal: Ni set a noon feast and again pledged grace and trust (text may corrupt ‘set up’ as ‘kill’).
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni then gave them a midday feast and renewed his promises of goodwill.

sentences.zh: 遂獲鹽鐵，器用周贍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they obtained salt and iron; implements and uses were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron flowed again, and supplies grew plentiful.

sentences.zh: 漢嘉郡界旄牛夷種類四千餘戶，其率狼路，欲為姑婿冬逢報怨。

translations.literal: Within Hanjia Commandery the Maoniu Yi sorts were more than four thousand households; their chief Langlu wished to avenge his sister's husband Dong Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand Maoniu households in Hanjia followed chief Langlu, who meant to avenge his brother-in-law Dong Feng.

sentences.zh: 遣叔父離將，逢眾相度形勢。

translations.literal: He sent uncle Li to lead; Feng's multitude surveyed the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his uncle Li at the head of Dong Feng’s followers to scout the ground.

sentences.zh: 嶷逆遣親近繼牛酒勞賜，又令離姊逆逢妻宣暢意旨。

translations.literal: Ni in advance sent intimates following with cattle and wine as labor reward; also ordered Li's elder sister, Feng's wife, to proclaim and extend intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni preempted him with cattle and wine sent through trusted agents and had Li’s sister—Dong Feng’s widow—carry his terms.

sentences.zh: 離既受賜，並見其姊，姊弟歡悅，悉率所領將詣嶷，嶷厚加賞待，遣還。

translations.literal: Li having received the gifts and also seeing his elder sister, elder sister and younger brother rejoiced; they all led those they commanded and generals to Ni; Ni richly rewarded and treated them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Li accepted the gifts, met his sister, and the siblings persuaded their followers to visit Zhang Ni, who rewarded them generously and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 旄牛由是輒不為患。

translations.literal: Maoniu from this often did not become a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The Maoniu tribes ceased to be a threat.

sentences.zh: 郡有舊道，經旄牛中至成都，既平且近。

translations.literal: The commandery had an old road passing through Maoniu to Chengdu, both level and near.
translations.idiomatic: An old road once ran through Maoniu to Chengdu—level and short.

sentences.zh: 自旄牛絕道，已百餘年，更由安上，既險且遠。

translations.literal: Since Maoniu cut the road, already more than a hundred years, one instead goes by Anshang—both perilous and far.
translations.idiomatic: For a century the Maoniu stretch had been closed, forcing travelers onto the long, dangerous Anshang detour.

sentences.zh: 疑遣左右資貨幣賜路，重令路姑喻意，路乃率兄弟妻子悉詣疑，疑與盟誓，開通舊道，千里肅清，復古亭繹。

translations.literal: Ni sent attendants with goods and currency to bestow on Langlu, again ordered Langlu's aunt to convey intent; Langlu thereupon led brothers, wives, and children all to Ni; Ni swore covenant with them, opened and cleared the old road; a thousand li were solemnly cleared; restored ancient posts and relays.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni sent gifts to Langlu through his aunt until Langlu brought his whole household in to swear allegiance. They reopened the old road, cleared a thousand li of trouble, and restored the postal stations.

sentences.zh: 奏封路為旋牛毗王，遣使將路朝貢。

translations.literal: He memorialized Langlu as king of the Maoniu tribes and sent envoys to bring him to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained an edict naming Langlu king of the Maoniu people and escorted him to Chengdu to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 後主於是加疑撫戎將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: The Later Lord thereupon added Ni as general who pacifies the Rong, holding the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then added Zhang Ni the title General Who Pacifies the Rong while he continued as administrator.

sentences.zh: 嶷初見費禕為大將軍，恣性泛愛，待信新附不過，嶷書戒之曰：「昔岑彭率師，來歙杖節，咸見害於刺客，今明將軍位尊權重，宜鑒前事，少以為警。

translations.literal: When Ni first saw Fei Yi as grand general, indulgent nature broadly loving, treating and trusting new adherents without limit, Ni wrote warning him, saying, "Formerly Cen Peng led troops, Lai She bore the staff of authority—both were harmed by assassins; now enlightened lord general rank is esteemed and power heavy; ought to mirror former affairs and take little as warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei Yi became grand general, Zhang Ni saw him trusting new allies too freely and wrote: "Cen Peng and Lai She died by assassins’ blades; your station is still higher—learn from them and stay guarded.

sentences.zh: 」後禕果為魏降人郭脩所害。

translations.literal: " Later Yi indeed was harmed by Wei surrendered man Guo Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei Yi was indeed murdered soon after by the Wei defector Guo Xiu.

sentences.zh: 吳太傅諸葛恪以初破魏軍，大興兵眾以圖攻取。

translations.literal: Wu grand tutor Zhuge Ke because he had first broken Wei troops, greatly raised troops and masses planning attack and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Elated by his first victory over Wei, Wu’s Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke mobilized a massive host for further conquests.

sentences.zh: 侍中諸葛瞻，丞相亮之子，恪從弟也。

translations.literal: The palace attendant Zhuge Zhan, Chancellor Liang's son, was Ke's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhuge Zhan—Zhuge Liang’s son and Zhuge Ke’s cousin—was the man to receive the letter.

sentences.zh: 嶷與書曰：

translations.literal: Ni wrote to him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni wrote to him:

sentences.zh: 東主初崩，帝實幼弱，太傅受寄託之重，亦何容易！

translations.literal: The eastern lord has just passed; the emperor is truly young and weak; the grand tutor bears the heavy burden of entrustment—is it easy!
translations.idiomatic: Your sovereign has just died, the boy emperor is frail, and the Grand Tutor shoulders the whole regency—nothing about this moment is safe.

sentences.zh: 親以周公之才，猶有管、蔡流言之變，霍光受任，亦有燕、蓋、上官逆亂之謀，賴成、昭之明，以免斯難耳。

translations.literal: Even with the Duke of Zhou's talent, still there was Guan and Cai's slanderous rumor change; Huo Guang received appointment, still there were Yan, Gai, and Shangguan's rebellion plots—relying on Cheng and Zhao's clarity to escape this hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou faced the rebellion of his brothers; Huo Guang endured plots from princes and ministers until sober rulers restored order.

sentences.zh: 昔每聞東主殺生賞罰，不任下人，又今以垂沒之命，卒召太傅，屬以後事，誠實可慮。

translations.literal: Formerly I often heard the eastern lord on killing life reward punishment did not trust inferiors; moreover now with dying-out mandate suddenly summoned the grand tutor and entrusted latter affairs—truly it is to be worried.
translations.idiomatic: Your late ruler trusted no one with life-and-death authority; on his deathbed he summoned the Grand Tutory alone—that legacy invites peril.

sentences.zh: 加吳、楚剽急，乃昔所記，而太傅離少主，履敵庭，恐非良計長算之術也。

translations.literal: Add Wu and Chu are rash and urgent—as ancient records note—and the grand tutor leaves the young lord and treads the enemy court; I fear this is not good planning long reckoning art.
translations.idiomatic: Wu men are famously rash; for the regent to march deep into enemy lands while the orphan sovereign stays home is no sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 雖云東家綱紀肅然，上下輯睦，百有一失，非明者之慮邪？

translations.literal: Although they say the eastern house discipline is solemn, high and low harmonize—of a hundred there is one failure—is it not the wise man's worry?
translations.idiomatic: They tell you eastern Wu is orderly—yet even perfect discipline admits one slip in a hundred; surely a thoughtful man guards against it?

sentences.zh: 取古則今，今則古也，自非郎君進忠言於太傅，誰復有盡言者也！

translations.literal: Take antiquity as norm for today; today then is antiquity—unless you, young lord, advance loyal words to the grand tutor, who again will have exhaustive words!
translations.idiomatic: History judges present failures by ancient precedent—if you do not speak plainly to your cousin, who will?

sentences.zh: 旋軍廣農，務行德惠，數年之中，東西並舉，實為不晚，願深採察。

translations.literal: Turn the army and broaden agriculture; devote effort to practicing virtue and kindness; within several years east and west together rise—it truly is not late; wish deeply adopt and examine.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw the army, enrich the farms, and win hearts with kindness—within a few years you might strike east and west together; it would not be too late. Please weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 恪竟以此夷族。

translations.literal: Ke in the end by this exterminated the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke ignored the warning and his whole clan was slaughtered for it.

sentences.zh: 嶷識見多如是類。

translations.literal: Ni’s insight and vision were many of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni’s foresight often ran this true.

sentences.zh: 在郡十五年，邦域安穆。

translations.literal: In the commandery fifteen years, the state domain was peaceful and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen years he governed Yuexi in quiet order.

sentences.zh: 屢乞求還，乃徵詣成都。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he begged to return; thereupon he was summoned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He begged repeatedly to come home until the court recalled him to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 夷民戀慕，扶轂泣涕，過旄牛邑，邑君襁負來迎，及追尋至蜀郡界，其督相率隨嶷朝貢者百餘人。

translations.literal: Yi people clung and longed; they held carriage hubs and wept tears; passing Maoniu town the district lord came carrying children on back to welcome; reaching as far as Shu Commandery border, their overseers leading one another following Ni to court tribute were more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Tribesmen clung to his wheels in tears; the Maoniu headman brought infants on his back to greet him; more than a hundred chiefs followed him to the Shu border to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 嶷至，拜蕩寇將軍，慷慨壯烈，士人咸多貴之。

translations.literal: When Ni arrived he was appointed general who sweeps bandits; impassioned and fierce, gentlemen all greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was named General Who Sweeps the Raiders—fiery and outspoken, and the Ru scholars admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 然放蕩少禮，人亦以此譏焉，

translations.literal: Yet unrestrained and lacking rites, people also by this mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Others mocked him for loose manners and blunt ceremony.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：時車騎將軍夏侯霸謂嶷曰：「雖與足下疏闊，然託心如舊，宜明此意。

translations.literal: < The Biographies of the Elders of Yi records: At that time general of chariots and cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Ni, "Although with you I am distant and broad, yet entrusting heart is as of old—ought to clarify this intent.
translations.idiomatic: < The Yi elders relate that General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba told Zhang Ni: "We seldom meet, yet I trust you as an old friend—let there be no misunderstanding between us.

sentences.zh: 」嶷答曰：「僕未知子，子未知我，大道在彼，何云託心乎！

translations.literal: " Ni replied, saying, "I do not yet know you, you do not yet know me; the great way lies there—what speak of entrusting heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Ni answered: "You do not know me, nor I you—how can we speak of sworn hearts while higher duty still stands between us?

sentences.zh: 原三年之後徐陳斯言。

translations.literal: Let after three years slowly set forth these words.
translations.idiomatic: Ask me again in three years and we may speak of friendship.

sentences.zh: 」有識之士以為美談。〉

translations.literal: " Men of insight took it as fine discourse.>
translations.idiomatic: " Thoughtful men praised the exchange as exemplary.>

sentences.zh: 是歲延熙十七年也。

translations.literal: This year was Yanxi seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: That was the seventeenth year of Yanxi (254).

sentences.zh: 魏狄道長李簡密書請降，衛將軍姜維率嶷等因簡之資以出隴西。

translations.literal: Wei Didao chief Li Jian secret letter requested surrender; General of the Guard Jiang Wei led Ni and others relying on Jian's resources to exit Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jian, magistrate of Wei’s Didao, secretly offered to defect, Jiang Wei marched west with Zhang Ni and used Li’s stores to open a route into Longxi.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷風濕固疾，至都浸篤，扶杖然後能起。

translations.literal: < The Biographies of the Elders of Yi records: Ni had rheumatism chronic illness; arriving at the capital it worsened gradually; leaning on a staff then could rise.
translations.idiomatic: < The tradition adds that chronic rheumatism left Zhang Ni barely able to rise without a staff once he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 李簡請降，眾議狐疑，而嶷曰必然。

translations.literal: Li Jian requested surrender; crowd deliberation was fox-suspicious; yet Ni said inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion doubted Li Jian’s offer; Zhang Ni alone insisted it was genuine.

sentences.zh: 姜維之出，時論以嶷初還，股疾不能在行中，由是嶷自乞肆力中原，致身敵庭。

translations.literal: When Jiang Wei marched out, current opinion held that Ni had just returned and thigh illness could not be in the ranks; thereby Ni himself begged to exert strength in the Central Plain and offer body in the enemy court.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei marched, others argued Zhang Ni was too lame from his recent return to ride with the army—so Zhang Ni volunteered to serve in the interior, striking deep into enemy territory despite his legs.

sentences.zh: 臨發，辭後主曰：「臣當值聖明，受恩過量，加以疾病在身，常恐一朝隕沒，辜負榮遇。

translations.literal: On the point of setting out, he took leave of the Later Lord, saying, "I have met a sage and enlightened ruler; I have received favor beyond measure; added to this is illness in my person—I always fear that one morning I will fall and perish and betray honored favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army marched he bade the emperor farewell: "I have served a wise master and received more favor than I deserve, yet I am ill and fear I may die overnight and fail that trust.

sentences.zh: 天不違原，得豫戎事。

translations.literal: Heaven does not oppose my wish; I have been able to take part in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has granted my prayer to share in this campaign (the clause reads ‘does not oppose yuan,’ parallel to editions that say Heaven did not refuse me).

sentences.zh: 若涼州克定，臣為籓表守將；

translations.literal: If Liang Province is taken and settled, I shall be a garrison general guarding the outer frontier.
translations.idiomatic: If we conquer Liangzhou, let me hold its march as your frontier warden.

sentences.zh: 若有未捷，殺身以報。

translations.literal: If there is not yet victory, I will kill my person to repay.
translations.idiomatic: If we fall short, I will lay down my life to repay you.

sentences.zh: 」後主慨然為之流涕。〉

translations.literal: " The Later Lord sighed and for it shed tears.>
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept at his words.>

sentences.zh: 既到狄道，簡悉率城中吏民出迎軍。

translations.literal: When they reached Didao, Jian led all the officials and people of the city out to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei reached Didao, Li Jian brought officials and townsfolk out to greet the Shu army.

sentences.zh: 軍前與魏將徐質交鋒，嶷臨陣隕身，然其所殺傷亦過倍。

translations.literal: The army front crossed spears with Wei general Xu Zhi; Ni fell in the line of battle, yet those he killed and wounded were also more than doubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the clash with Wei’s Xu Zhi, Zhang Ni died on the field yet killed more than twice his own losses.

sentences.zh: 既亡，封長子瑛西鄉侯，次子護雄襲爵。

translations.literal: When he had died, the eldest son Ying was enfeoffed marquis of Xixiang; the second son Huxiong inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his eldest son Zhang Ying was made Marquis of Xixiang; the younger son Zhang Huxiong inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 南土越崔巂民夷聞嶷死，無不悲泣，為嶷立廟，四時水旱輒祀之。

translations.literal: In the southern lands the Yue-Cui peoples and Yi heard Ni had died; none did not grieve and weep; they erected a temple for Ni; at the four seasons, flood and drought, they always sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Across the southern frontier—in Yuexi and neighboring valleys—settlers and tribes alike mourned Zhang Ni, raised shrines to him, and prayed to him whenever drought or flood threatened.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：余觀張嶷儀貌辭令，不能駭人，而其策略足以入算，果烈足以立威，為臣有忠誠之節，處類有亮直之風，而動必顧典，後主深崇之。

translations.literal: < The Biographies of the Elders of Yi records: I observed Zhang Ni's bearing and speech—they cannot awe people—but his stratagems suffice to enter reckoning; decisiveness suffices to establish awe; as minister he had loyalty and fidelity; among peers he had bright straightness; in movement he always consulted precedent—the Later Lord deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: < The compiler writes: Zhang Ni cut an undistinguished figure, yet his schemes were sound, his blows decisive, his loyalty absolute, his manner bluntly honest, and every deed weighed against precedent—the emperor esteemed him above many flashier men.

sentences.zh: 雖古之英士，何以遠逾哉！

translations.literal: Even ancient heroes—how could they far surpass!
translations.idiomatic: The heroes of antiquity scarcely surpassed him!

sentences.zh: 《蜀世譜》曰：嶷孫奕，晉梁州刺史。〉

translations.literal: The Shu Shifu records: Ni's grandson Yi was Jin's provincial governor of Liang.>
translations.idiomatic: The Shu genealogical tables add that his grandson Zhang Yi governed Liangzhou under Western Jin.>

sentences.zh: 【評價】

translations.literal: [Evaluator's commentary]
translations.idiomatic: Historian’s appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：黃權弘雅思量，李恢公亮志業，呂凱守節不回，馬忠擾而能毅，

translations.literal: The evaluation says: Huang Quan was broad and refined in thought and capacity; Li Hui was fair, bright in aim and enterprise; Lü Kai kept integrity and did not turn back; Ma Zhong was compliant yet able to be resolute,
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict: Huang Quan combined breadth with judgment; Li Hui pursued an honorable career; Lü Kai held firm without wavering; Ma Zhong was supple yet resolute,

sentences.zh: 〈《尚書》曰：擾而毅。

translations.literal: < The Documents says: compliant yet resolute.
translations.idiomatic: < as the Shangshu puts it: gentle in manner, firm in deed.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：擾，馴也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: compliant means tame.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses ‘compliant’ as tractable.

sentences.zh: 致果曰毅。〉

translations.literal: Achieving decisive outcome is called resolute.>
translations.idiomatic: ‘Resolute’ means carrying an attack through to victory.>

sentences.zh: 王平忠勇而嚴整，張嶷識斷明果，咸以所長，顯名發跡，遇其時也。

translations.literal: Wang Ping was loyal and brave and strict and orderly; Zhang Ni's knowledge and judgment were clear and decisive—all by what they were long at displayed name and rose from traces—they met their times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping married loyalty and courage to iron discipline; Zhang Ni paired sharp insight with bold execution. Each rose to fame through his strengths when fate gave him the opening.
